header: Managing custom plugins using the AWS CLI
content:
You can use the AWS CLI to manage a number of custom plugin tasks.
Tasks
• Installing a custom plugin using the AWS CLI
• Updating a custom plugin using the AWS CLI
• Create or update a custom plugin with an AWS KMS key security
• Upgrading an OpenSearch Service domain with custom plugins to a later version of OpenSearch
using the AWS CLI
• Uninstalling and viewing the dissociation status of a custom plugin
Installing a custom plugin using the AWS CLI
Before you begin
Before you can associate a custom plugin with your domain, you must upload it to an Amazon
Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket. The bucket must be located in the same AWS Region
where you intend to use the plugin. For information about adding an object to an S3 bucket, see
Uploading objects in the Amazon Simple Storage Service User Guide.
If your plugin contains sensitive information, specify server-side encryption with S3-managed
keys when you upload it. After you upload the ﬁle, make note of its S3 path. The path format is
s3://amzn-s3-demo-bucket/file-path/file-name.
Custom plugins
1492
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Developer Guide
Note
You can optionally secure a custom plugin when you create the plugin by specifying an
AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. For information, see the section called
“Create or update a custom plugin with an AWS KMS key security”.
To install a custom plugin using the AWS CLI
1.
Create a new package for your custom plugin by running the following create-package
command, ensuring that the following requirements are met:
• The bucket and key location must point to the plugin .zip ﬁle in an S3 bucket in the
account in which your are running the commands.
• The S3 bucket must be in the same Region where the package is being created.
• Only .zip ﬁles are supported for ZIP-PLUGIN packages.
• The contents of the .zip ﬁle must follow directory structure as expected by the plugin.
• The value for --engine-version must be in the format
OpenSearch_{MAJOR}.{MINOR}. For example: OpenSearch_2.17.
Replace the placeholder values with your own information:
aws opensearch create-package \
--package-name package-name \
--region region \
--package-type ZIP-PLUGIN \
--package-source S3BucketName=amzn-s3-demo-bucket,S3Key=s3-key \
--engine-version opensearch-version
2.
(Optional) View the status of the create-package operation, including any validation
and security vulnerability ﬁndings, by using the describe-packages command. Replace the
placeholder values with your own information:
aws opensearch describe-packages \
--region region  \
--filters '[{"Name": "PackageType","Value": ["ZIP-PLUGIN"]}, {"Name":
"PackageName","Value": ["package-name"]}]'
Custom plugins
1493
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Developer Guide
The command returns information similar to the following:
{
"PackageDetailsList": [{
"PackageID": "pkg-identifier",
"PackageName": "package-name",
"PackageType": "ZIP-PLUGIN",
"PackageStatus": "VALIDATION_FAILED",
"CreatedAt": "2024-11-11T13:07:18.297000-08:00",
"LastUpdatedAt": "2024-11-11T13:10:13.843000-08:00",
"ErrorDetails": {
"ErrorType": "",
"ErrorMessage": "PluginValidationFailureReason : Dependency Scan
reported 3 vulnerabilities for the plugin: CVE-2022-23307, CVE-2019-17571,
CVE-2022-23305"
},
"EngineVersion": "OpenSearch_2.15",
"AllowListedUserList": [],
"PackageOwner": "OWNER-XXXX"
}]
}
Note
During the create-package operation, Amazon OpenSearch Service checks the ZIP-
PLUGIN value for version compatibility, supported plugin extensions, and security
vulnerabilities. The security vulnerabilities are scanned using the Amazon Inspector
service. The results of these checks are shown in ErrorDetails ﬁeld in the API
response.
3.
Use the associate-package command to associate the plugin with the OpenSearch Service
domain of your choice using the package ID of the package created in the previous step.
Tip
If you have multiple plugins, you can instead use the associate-packages command to
associate multiple packages to a domain in single operation.
Custom plugins
1494
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Developer Guide
Replace the placeholder values with your own information:
aws opensearch associate-package \
--domain-name domain-name \
--region region \
--package-id package-id
Note
The plugin is installed and uninstalled using a blue/green deployment process.
4.
(Optional) Use the list-packages-for-domain command to view the status of the association.
The association status changes as the workﬂow progresses from ASSOCIATING to ACTIVE.
The association status changes to ACTIVE after the plugin installation completes and the
plugin is ready for use.
Replace the placeholder values with your own information.
aws opensearch list-packages-for-domain \
--region region \
--domain-name domain-name
Updating a custom plugin using the AWS CLI
Use the update-package command to make changes to a plugin.
Note
You can optionally secure a custom plugin when you update the plugin by specifying an
AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. For information, see the section called
“Create or update a custom plugin with an AWS KMS key security”.
To update a custom plugin using the AWS CLI
•
Run the following command. Replace the placeholder values with your own information.
Custom plugins
1495
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Developer Guide
aws opensearch update-package \
--region region \
--package-id package-id \
--package-source S3BucketName=amzn-s3-demo-bucket,S3Key=s3-key \
--package-description description
After updating a package, you can use the associate-package or associate-packages command to
apply package updates to a domain.
Note
You can audit, create, update, associate, and disassociate operations on the plugin using
AWS CloudTrail. For more information, see Monitoring Amazon OpenSearch Service API
calls with AWS CloudTrail.
Create or update a custom plugin with an AWS KMS key security
You can secure a custom plugin when you create or update the plugin by specifying an AWS KMS
key. To accomplish this, set PackageEncryptionOptions to true and specify the Amazon
Resource Name (ARN) of the key, as shown in the following examples.
Example: Create a custom plugin with AWS KMS key security
aws opensearch create-package \
--region us-east-2  --package-name my-custom-package \
--package-type ZIP-PLUGIN \
--package-source S3BucketName=amzn-s3-demo-bucket,S3Key=my-s3-key
--engine-version OpenSearch_2.15
"PackageConfigOptions": {
...
}
"PackageEncryptionOptions": {
"Enabled": true,
"KmsKeyId":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-2:111222333444:key/2ba228d5-1d09-456c-ash9-
daf42EXAMPLE"
}
Example: Update a custom plugin with AWS KMS key security

1496
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Developer Guide
aws opensearch update-package \
--region us-east-2  --package-name my-custom-package \
--package-type ZIP-PLUGIN \
--package-source S3BucketName=amzn-s3-demo-bucket,S3Key=my-s3-key
--engine-version OpenSearch_2.15
"PackageConfigOptions": {
...
}
"PackageEncryptionOptions": {
"Enabled": true,
"KmsKeyId":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-2:111222333444:key/2ba228d5-1d09-456c-ash9-
daf42EXAMPLE"
}
Important
If the AWS KMS key you specify is disabled or deleted, it can leave the associated cluster
inoperational.
For more information about AWS KMS integration with custom packages, the section called
“Amazon OpenSearch Service custom package AWS KMS integration”.
Upgrading an OpenSearch Service domain with custom plugins to a later version of
OpenSearch using the AWS CLI
When you need to upgrade an OpenSearch Service domain that uses custom plugins to a later
version of OpenSearch, complete the following processes.
To upgrade an OpenSearch Service domain with custom plugins to a later version of
OpenSearch using the AWS CLI
1.
Use the create-package command to create a new package for your plugin specifying the new
OpenSearch version.
Ensure that package name is the same for the plugin for all engine versions. Changing the
package name causes the domain upgrade process to fail during the blue/green deployment.
2.
Upgrade your domain to the higher version by following the steps in the section called
“Upgrading domains”.
Custom plugins
1497
Amazon OpenSearch Service
Developer Guide
During this process, Amazon OpenSearch Service disassociates the previous version of the
plugin package and installs the new version using a blue/green deployment.
Uninstalling and viewing the dissociation status of a custom plugin
To uninstall the plugin from any domain, you can use the dissociate-package command. Running
this command also removes any related conﬁguration or license packages. You can then use the
list-packages-for-domain command to view the status of the dissociation.
Tip
You can also use dissociate-packages command to uninstall multiple plugins from a domain
in a single operation.
To uninstall and view the dissociation status of a custom plugin
1.
Disable the plugin in every index. This must be done before you dissociate the plugin package.
If you try to uninstall a plugin before disabling it from every index, the blue/green deployment
process remains stuck in the Processing state.
2.
Run the following command to uninstall the plugin. Replace the placeholder values with
your own information.
aws opensearch dissociate-package \
--region region \
--package-id plugin-package-id \
--domain-name domain name
3.
(Optional) Run the list-packages-for-domain command to view the status of the dissociation.
